"Any non-zero vector is an eigenvector of A because A times a vector gives a vector." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: An eigenvector must satisfy Av = λv: its image is parallel to v. Most vectors change direction under A.

Each year 5% of members who use the gym change so that they use the pool, and 25% of those who use the pool change so that they use the gym; the total of 2300 members is constant. (a) Write down the transition matrix T. (b) Show that the eigenvalues of T are 1 and 0.7. (c) Find the eigenvector for λ = 1 and hence the long-term numbers using each. (d) Explain, using the second eigenvalue, why the numbers approach this steady state.
items.markingKey: (a) A1. (b) det(T − λI) = λ² − 1.7λ + 0.7 (M1) = (λ − 1)(λ − 0.7) (A1, AG). (c) (T − I)v = 0 ⇒ v ∝ (0.25, 0.05) (M1 A1); scale to total 2300: (1920, 383) (A1). (d) R1 xₙ = c₁(1)ⁿv₁ + c₂(0.7)ⁿv₂ and the second term decays to 0.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "eigenvalue"?

The number of rows × the number of columns, m × n
A scalar λ for which Av = λv has a non-zero solution v; found from det(A − λI) = 0
